title: Algerian Lamb Tagine
description: A traditional Algerian dish featuring lamb, spices, and dried fruits, resulting in a jammy and crumbly texture, this recipe is Jain-friendly and does not include any animal by-products or root vegetables.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until it is softened and lightly browned.
Add the ground lamb and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until it is no longer pink.
Add the dried apricots, prunes, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt, and pepper, and stir to combine.
Add the water to the pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 1 1/2 hours.
Uncover the pot and continue to simmer for an additional 30 minutes, or until the sauce has thickened and the meat is tender.
Serve the tagine hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley or cilantro.
Traditionally, the tagine is cooked in a clay pot with a conical lid, which allows the steam to condense and drop back into the pot, resulting in a tender and flavorful dish.
To achieve a similar effect, you can cover the pot with foil and then a lid, or use a slow cooker.
